newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas slips late on technical selling.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas slips late on technical selling.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures slipped late Wednesday in fairly active trade, pressured by some technical selling and long liquidation after upside momentum stalled early in the session, source said.
At 1425 EDT, July slipped 3.1 cents to $2.255 per million British thermal units, while August was 3.4 cents lower at $2.235. Most other deferreds were down by one to two cents.

"We tried to break $2.30 (basis July) and briefly succeeded, but it didn't set off any chain reaction and opened the door to the sellers," said one Midwest trader, adding he saw more price pressure ahead.

While some unplanned nuclear plant outages and scorching heat in the Midwest and East this week gave a boost to the market ahead of bidweek this week, many now were hard-pressed for reasons to move much higher.
"All the good news is in the price, but with storage comfortable, at some point, people are going to start selling into the (hot) weather," the Midwest trader said.
One producer agreed, adding "There seems to be a real reluctance to pay any premium for July gas in the cash. I'm getting real negative on the physical market."

In the East, unplanned outages were reported this week at PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1, GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 and Duke's 846 MW Oconee 3. All were expected to remain off line until early next week.

The region already was vulnerable to power spikes, with extended shutdowns at two Salem units in New Jersey and three Millstone units in Conn. as well as maintenance outages at the two Indian Point units in New York. The Indian Point units are expected back next month.
While more seasonal temperatures were expected in the Northeast by the weekend, warmer weather was forecast for early next week.
A Reuter poll showed most expected a weekly gas stock build in the 85-90 bcf range when the AGA report is issued later today. For the same week last year, stocks gained 91 bcf.

Chart traders said July's close Tuesday above downtrend resistance turned the technical picture more positive, with a test of the $2.36-2.37 area possible, but with six straight up days, they said most of the shorts may already have covered. Further resistance was seen at the contract high of $2.44. Support remained at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

With the spot month set to go off the board tomorrow, traders turned their attention to August, where the technical picture was clouded by the contract's failure this week to close above the intermediate down trendline. Trendline resistance was seen at $2.28-2.29, with further selling likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.
Minor support in August was pegged at $2.235, with better buying expected at $2.145 and then at the recent $2.08 low.

In the cash Tuesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices were talked little changed in the high-$2.20s. Midcon pipes also held steady in the low-teens. New York city gate gas was quoted higher early in the high-$2.60s, then slipped back later to about unchanged in the low-$2.60s.
NYMEX said 36,251 contracts traded at 1335 EDT.
On the KCBT, July edged 0.1 cent higher to $2.15, while deferreds were steady to down 2.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 3.2 cents to 10.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT July natgas futures expire today.
